problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Shipment Alpha: size 61 cubic meters
* Shipment Beta: size 42 cubic meters
* Shipment Gamma: size 63 cubic meters
* Shipment Delta: size 48 cubic meters
* Shipment Epsilon: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment Zeta: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment Eta: size 35 cubic meters
* Shipment Theta: size 39 cubic meters
* Shipment Iota: size 53 cubic meters
* Shipment Kappa: size 64 cubic meters
* Shipment Lambda: size 30 cubic meters
* Shipment Mu: size 69 cubic meters
* Shipment Nu: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Xi: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment Omicron: size 64 cubic meters
* Shipment Pi: size 44 cubic meters
* Shipment Rho: size 67 cubic meters
* Shipment Sigma: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment Tau: size 30 cubic meters
* Shipment Upsilon: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment Phi: size 56 cubic meters
* Shipment Chi: size 52 cubic meters
* Shipment Psi: size 34 cubic meters
* Shipment Omega: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment A1: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment B1: size 52 cubic meters
* Shipment C1: size 36 cubic meters
* Shipment D1: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment E1: size 66 cubic meters
* Shipment F1: size 39 cubic meters
* Shipment G1: size 52 cubic meters

Each cargo plane has a maximum capacity of 100 cubic meters. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes possible. Every shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume of shipments on any plane cannot exceed its capacity limit.
